headline: 68 dead as high-speed trains collide in Spain, 80 injured
summary: The crash is the deadliest train accident in Europe since 2013, occurring in the Castilla-La Mancha region.
details: A high-speed passenger train collided with a stationary train in rural Castilla-La Mancha, Spain, leaving 68 people dead and 80 others injured.
Of the injured, 15 are reported to be in critical condition. Rescue workers continue to search for more bodies among the mangled wreckage of the carriages.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed deep grief and promised a full investigation into the cause of the crash, stating that two high-speed rail accidents in one year are unacceptable.
Transport Minister Oscar Puente stated that the Renfe-operated train had been given a red signal, but was permitted to proceed despite the signal being active.
A computer communication system error caused the red signal, and while the train was automatically stopped, the decision to allow it to to proceed was described as a 'mistake'.
Renfe stated that their train collided with an Iryo-operated train that was stationary, though they have not yet determined why the Iryo train was stopped.
Survivors described harrowing experiences, with some passengers having to break windows to escape while others were trapped in their seats.
Renfe has suspended ticket sales for the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail route until December 13, and a special hotline has been launched for families of the victims.
This is the second deadly high-speed rail accident in Spain this year, following a January crash that killed 46 people, raising concerns about rail infrastructure investment.

headline: World Bank: Commodity prices could rise 23% by year-end
summary: Global conflicts and the El Niño weather phenomenon are driving up fuel and food costs, risking higher inflation and food insecurity.
details: The World Bank warns that global commodity prices could surge by 23% by the end of this year. This spike is driven by rising fuel costs due to conflicts involving Iran and food price hikes linked to global tensions and El Niño.
